title: People illustration / Rose and Almond — RGB palette

location.series: IBM Design Language / alternate tab states
location.label: RGB

slide_intent: Represent people with a deliberately scoped palette, because human diversity requires more than reusing the main brand’s accent colors.
strategic_value: Two organized skin-tone families can help IBM portray people consistently while keeping human representation distinct from its general palette.
demonstration: The RGB tab shows two dark-to-light columns, Rose and Almond, each with ten named grades and channel values.
practical_value: Select RGB skin, hair or nail colors from the people palette while retaining the source’s limited application scope.

content_islands.name: Encoding selector
content_islands.spec: Show RGB selected beside HEX and CMYK.

content_islands.name: Rose family
content_islands.spec: Arrange Rose 100 through Rose 10 in the left column with red/green/blue values.

content_islands.name: Almond family
content_islands.spec: Align Almond 100 through Almond 10 in the right column with matching grade order.

ingredient.name: Rose and Almond people palette
ingredient.role: Represent varied human appearances within IBM illustration.
ingredient.application: Choose the relevant Rose or Almond grade for skin, hair and nails; use the listed RGB values for digital work.
ingredient.scope: The People page explicitly limits this palette to skin, hair and nails. Do not generalize it into a main-brand accent palette.

reference_purposes.Intent: The accompanying People palette text connects the two families to ethnic and geographic diversity.
reference_purposes.Expression: Rose and Almond provide a structured warm-toned range separate from the main IBM palette.
reference_purposes.Application: The RGB values make the people palette usable in digital illustrations.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The accompanying text reserves this palette for skin, hair and nails and says it is not an extension of the main palette.
